answer.evidence: Rows 0-14 form a large roof plane of three paneled doors, blue and white above and green and red below. They end at a lighter brown beam or edge line on row 15, followed by dark eave shadow on rows 16-17. The pallet front wall below runs from row 17 to row 30 (14 rows), with slats and a dark entrance gap. The roof is a deep top surface above a clear front face, not a rim or a flat band.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is tiny next to the references: about 48x28 source px, versus whole houses with full scalloped roofs. The measured facts are fine. It has 18 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10, 4% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edges, so its outlines are tinted and not a black sticker line. By eye, though, each material ramp is shallow. The three door roof panels are mostly one flat tone each, with a lighter top edge and a dark lower edge, giving about 3 steps. The pallet wall is a few brown stripes with little per-plank grain. The sack and the dark entrance are small blobs. The references have 5-6 step tile ramps with per-tile highlights, plaster speckle, and individually shaded stones. This piece reads as a small, simplified sprite and falls short of that craft level. The panel details (paneled-door insets) are only hinted at. When in doubt, fail.
